findings.summary: The media-retention and storage statements are placed together without a table row, and the 1 PB/day media figure sits alongside a claim that media does not pile up, which is not quantified.
findings.evidence: "Media is stored briefly, so it does not pile up forever" (no retention period; page 10 says ~30 days)
findings.fix: State the ~30-day retention here and add a Retention row to the scale table so the pages agree.

findings.summary: Redis session commands are shown as code with only a one-line caption, and the same session SET/EXPIRE snippet is repeated on pages 2 and 3.
findings.evidence: bash SET session:42 gw-17 EX 60 / GET session:42 / EXPIRE session:42 60 (page 2) and redis SET session:{user_id} gw-417 EX 60 (page 3)
findings.fix: Keep the snippet on one page (the gateway page) and reference it from the other. State the TTL-plus-heartbeat idea as a bullet before the code.

findings.summary: Group fan-out tasks are said to be partitioned by group_id, but the rest of the chapter partitions Kafka by conversation_id, and the page never says the two are the same key.
findings.evidence: "Publish a delivery task per member to Kafka, partitioned by group_id" versus "Kafka partitioned by conversation_id" (page 2) and "Kafka partition by conversation_id keeps that order" (page 11)
findings.fix: Partition by conversation_id, or add a line saying a group's group_id is its conversation_id, so the per-group order guarantee on page 11 clearly follows from the partition key.

findings.summary: The 'Why fan out on the server' table is a comparison, but the group-data bullets mix the join-history rule and the SQL schema without a stated idea first.
findings.evidence: "A member added later gets history only from the join point" / "The join event stores join_seq; history reads start at seq >= join_seq" followed by the groups(...) SQL
findings.fix: Put a single-line statement of the membership model before the SQL and split the join rule into its own bullet.

findings.summary: The APNs/FCM table has identical content in both columns, so it conveys no comparison.
findings.evidence: Payload | small, no plaintext under E2EE | small, no plaintext under E2EE; Carries | wake signal + collapse key | wake signal + collapse key
findings.fix: Replace the table with a bullet saying both services carry the same small wake-up payload, or keep only the Platform row's difference.

findings.summary: Presence code appears after only a partial statement of the idea, and the heartbeat arithmetic is presented in a way that conflicts with the page 3 heartbeat load.
findings.evidence: "Heartbeats are ~500M sockets ÷ 30 s ≈ 17M refreshes/s at peak" vs page 3 "200K ÷ 30 s ≈ 6.7K pings/s" per node
findings.fix: Label the 17M/s figure as the fleet-wide total (~6.7K/s × 2,500 gateways) and call it average rather than peak, so the two pages read as consistent.

findings.summary: Several bullets hold more than one idea.
findings.evidence: "Not all contacts: 500 contacts × status flaps = fan-out storm"; "Online is shown at once; only offline is delayed"
findings.fix: Split each into separate one-idea bullets, one for the rule and one for its reason.

findings.summary: Dense bullets combine multiple ideas, and the JSON example appears before the stated idea of the key traveling inside the E2EE message.
findings.evidence: "Blobs expire after ~30 days; media is ~5% of messages, ~1 PB/day"; "Old keys are deleted, so a stolen key cannot decrypt past messages: forward secrecy"
findings.fix: Split into one fact per bullet and state the 'key travels inside the E2EE message' bullet before the JSON block.

findings.summary: The cheatsheet derives 500M concurrent sockets from '500M DAU online', which treats every daily active user as connected at the same instant.
findings.fix: State it as a deliberately conservative sizing assumption, for example 'assume peak concurrency equals DAU, an upper bound', or lower the concurrent figure.

findings.summary: The text uses a markdown heading, which the reader does not draw.
findings.evidence: # bug: new id on every attempt

findings.summary: A Check-yourself answer bundles several ideas into one bullet.
findings.evidence: "It creates 200 writes and 200 messages back to the sender, and receipts are already ~30% of traffic"
findings.fix: Split into separate bullets for the write cost, the return traffic and the existing receipt share.
